groups.title: the local readfirst command: argument parsing, git file listing, init/prompt/check/read/diff and the agent brief

checks.why: init, check, prompt, read and diff end to end on a scratch git repository

risks.text: src/action.mjs imports repoFiles, readMapFile and readText from cli.mjs, so changing how files are listed or the map is read also changes the GitHub Action
repoFiles lists untracked files that .gitignore does not exclude, so a stray scratch file in the working tree makes `check` fail and shows up in `diff`
parse() treats every --option except --json, --help and --force as taking a value, so a new on/off flag must be added to that list or it swallows the next argument
`check` reports map problems and exits 1, but prompt, read and diff go through loadMap and throw (exit 2 from bin) on any map problem, so a broken map blocks the read list completely
the pattern syntax in the agent brief must match what map.mjs accepts; if you change the pattern rules, update the brief as well

groups.title: the GitHub Action: one PR comment with the read list for the changed files, and a failed check when the map falls behind

checks.why: the Action against a fake GitHub API: post, update in place, broken map, read-only token, non-PR events

risks.text: composite actions do not set INPUT_* env vars, so action.yml maps each input to an env var by hand; a new input needs a line in action.yml and a read in action.mjs
the existing PR comment is found by its first line (MARKER); changing MARKER makes every open PR get a second comment instead of an update
a 403 from a comment write is treated as a fork PR and swallowed by matching ': 403 ' in the message built by api(); changing that error text turns fork PRs into failed jobs
the script runs only when argv[1] ends with '/src/action.mjs', and action.yml calls it by that path; moving or renaming the file makes the Action exit successfully without doing anything
when the map has problems the comment shows the problems but no read list, and the job fails unless fail-on-map-problems is 'false'

groups.title: the map format and checker, the first-draft map, import reading and the read list

checks.why: patterns, draft, check messages, imports and read list cases

risks.text: mapProblems rejects unknown fields, so a new map field must be added to the allowed-field list and made optional, and older readfirst versions will reject maps that use it; maps in users' repositories must keep passing under readfirst/map@1
the read list object is the --json output and what the Action renders; keep its field names and the readfirst/read-list@1 format string
patternToRegExp is used for group files, ignore, rule files and risk files alike; changing what a pattern matches moves files between groups in every user's map
test files are recognised by two separate regexes (isTest in readlist.mjs and the tests-folder check in draftMap); change both together

imports are read with regexes and only relative specifiers that resolve to a tracked file count, so path aliases and packages are not followed and tests reached through them are missing from the read list

groups.title: node:test suites for the command, the map, imports, the read list and the Action

risks.text: npm test only runs test/*.test.mjs, so a test in a subfolder or with another file name never runs
the CLI tests create and commit to real git repositories in the temp folder, so git must be on PATH
fakeGitHub answers any write it does not recognise with success, so a new GitHub API call in action.mjs passes unless a test asserts it
the tests assert exact markdown strings and draft group ids, so rewording toMarkdown or changing draftMap means updating these assertions and the README example

groups.title: package manifest, README, license and CI

risks.text: package.json "files" decides what npm ships (bin, src, README.md); a new folder under src ships automatically, a new top-level folder the command needs must be added there
package.json promises Node >=20 but CI tests only on Node 22, so a Node 22-only API passes CI and breaks for Node 20 users
CI's readfirst job runs this checkout's own Action (uses: ./), so every PR fails when a new file is not in .readfirst/map.json or when src/action.mjs is broken
the README repeats the command list, the Action inputs table and a sample read list; update it when cli.mjs HELP, action.yml inputs or toMarkdown output change

rules.rule: the readfirst command reads only the checkout: no network calls, no model calls, no API key
rules.why: it runs in agents' sandboxes and on private code; only the Action talks to the GitHub API

rules.rule: no runtime dependencies: Node's standard library only
rules.why: npx readfirst must start fast and nothing third-party runs on users' code

rules.rule: every tracked file is in exactly one group or in ignore, and every group and rule pattern matches a tracked file; check fails otherwise
rules.why: this is what stops the map from quietly falling behind the code

rules.rule: maps written for readfirst/map@1 keep passing: never rename or remove a map field or make an optional one required without a new format version
rules.why: map.json files live in users' repositories and CI fails on any map problem

rules.rule: the read list JSON keeps its field names under readfirst/read-list@1
rules.why: agents and tools read `readfirst read --json` and `diff --json`

rules.rule: only `readfirst init` writes a file, and it does not overwrite an existing map unless --force is given; check, prompt, read and diff never change the checkout
rules.why: agents run read and diff freely before every change

rules.rule: the Action keeps a single comment per PR and updates it in place on each push
rules.why: a new comment on every push floods the PR

rules.rule: a read-only token (PR from a fork) must not fail the Action: the read list goes to the job summary instead
rules.why: contributors from forks would otherwise get a red check they cannot fix

rules.rule: the Action takes the PR's changed files from the GitHub API, not from git history
rules.why: actions/checkout defaults to a shallow clone, so any checkout depth must work

rules.rule: the public code holds no hosted-version logic: the prompts and steps that fill the map stay on the server
rules.why: the free code is MIT and public; the paid value is the server's judgement. The hosted design lives in the private readfirst-cloud repository.
